newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen flat in slack trade.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen flat in slack trade.

text.p: Polish shares fell in lower trade on Tuesday and analysts expected them to stay virtually flat in low volumes during the two sessions between Christmas and the New Year.

The main market's WIG index fell 155.3 points, or 1.1 percent, to 14,165.5, and turnover fell 39.8 percent to 78.9 million zlotys ($27.2 million) on both markets as 58 issues fell, 10 rose and 15 were flat.
Analysts said investors were unlikely to open positions on Monday, when the bourse resumes trade, and on Tuesday.

"I think there could be a slight fall of less than one percent on Monday and also a limited movement of WIG index on Tuesday," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment Polska.
Analysts said if the central bank raised interest rates in January, as it warned on Monday, it could trigger falls.
They said paintmaker Polifarb Cieszyn fell 6.9 percent on profit-taking after surging 20.8 percent since Friday on a planned merger with Polifarb Wroclaw.
Polifarb Wroclaw slowed growth and rose 5.4 percent, after surging 26.8 percent since the plan was announced on Thursday.
Continuous trade turnover amounted to 6.2 million zlotys ($2.1 million) with five stocks rising and five staying flat.
Mass privatisation NFI units fell 5.4 percent in 11-million-zloty ($3.8 million) trade in regular session and fell 1.4 percent in 21.3-million-zloty ($7.3 million) continuous trade.
